steps.title: Imperatives
steps.html:
FormExample
Positivethe base verbPress the button.
NegativeDon't + base verbDon't press the button.
With a sequencerfirst / then / next / finallyFirst, take a clean glass.
Polite versionCould you…?Could you press the button?

The imperative is the same for one person or many. It never changes.

Use it for instructions, recipes, directions and warnings — not for asking a favour.

To ask a person politely, use the request forms from Lesson 11 instead.

steps.title: Three clips, thirty seconds each
steps.html:
1 · How to open a difficult jar. First, take a clean cloth and put it over the lid. Then hold the jar under hot water for ten seconds. Don't use cold water. Next, turn the lid slowly. Don't pull it. Finally, open it — easy!

2 · How to take a good photo of your food. First, put the plate next to a window. Don't stand in front of the light. Then turn the plate and find the best side. Next, hold the phone above the plate, not in front of it. Finally, press the button twice and choose the better photo.

3 · How to make your old bag look new. This one is easy and it's free. First, empty the bag. Then clean it with a soft cloth — don't wash it in the machine. Next, put paper inside it and leave it for a night. Finally, look at it in the morning. It isn't old-fashioned any more.
